story: Ebenezer Baptist Church was founded in 1886 by Pastor John A. Parker and eight people on Airline Street.
The church building was dedicated in 1922. Martin Luther King Jr. served as co-pastor with his father from 1960 until his assassination in 1968, and his funeral was held at Ebenezer on April 9, 1968.
The newer Horizon Sanctuary was inaugurated in 1999 with 1,700 seats, in the Martin Luther King Jr. National Historical Park.

stops.disputed: Wikipedia does not give the national park's founding year or the old sanctuary's style, so check the park's own history before repeating them.

story: The Georgia State Capitol was completed in March 1889. Willoughby J. Edbrooke and Franklin Pierce Burnham of Chicago designed it. Miles and Horne of Toledo handled construction. The style is Renaissance Revival and Classical Revival, modeled to resemble the U.S. Capitol.

The dome was gilded in a 1958 renovation with native gold leaf from near Dahlonega in Lumpkin County. The original dome was terra cotta covered with tin. A statue named Miss Freedom has stood on top since the building opened.
A convention voted in 1877 to move the state capital permanently to Atlanta, and the city handed over its City Hall tract in 1880. The Georgia Capitol Museum has existed inside since 1889.

stops.disputed: Wikipedia does not say whether the dome was gilded before 1958. Do not claim it was always gold.

The dome has always been covered in gold.

story: The Flatiron Building was built in 1897 and designed by Bradford Gilbert. It goes by several names: the English-American Building, the Georgia Savings Bank Building and the Empire Life Insurance Building.

It has 11 stories on a wedge-shaped block at 84 Peachtree Street NW, between Peachtree Street NE, Poplar Street NW and Broad Street NW. It was completed five years before New York's Flatiron Building and is described as the city's oldest standing skyscraper.
It was added to the National Register of Historic Places on March 26, 1976. It is now used for offices and includes a Microsoft Innovation Center.
stops.fact: It was finished five years before New York's Flatiron.
stops.disputed: "Oldest" depends on how you define a skyscraper. Wikipedia calls it the city's second and oldest standing one in the same description.

story: Piedmont Park covers 189 acres in Atlanta. It sits on the site of the 1895 Cotton States and International Exposition. The city bought the land in 1904, which extended the city limits to include the park and several developing neighborhoods.
The Olmsted Brothers offered a design between 1909 and 1912, and some of it was built. It includes Lake Clara Meer, an 11.5-acre lake.

The park gained a bathhouse, the Park Drive Bridge and Isamu Noguchi's Playscapes playground. After two decades of decline, the city adopted a master plan in 1982 and the Piedmont Park Conservancy formed in 1983. It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1976.
stops.disputed: The Olmsted plan was only partly built. Do not say the whole park follows it.
